newsitem.title: USA: American Home up on Premarin data.
newsitem.headline: American Home up on Premarin data.

text.p: Shares in American Home Products Corp rose on Tuesday amid expectations that generic competition for its Premarin estrogen replacement, the most widely prescribed drug in the U.S., could be further delayed.
But a spokeswoman for Duramed Pharmaceuticals Inc said the company was "tremendously confident" it would soon get FDA backing for a cut-priced version of the drug.
An American Home spokeswoman said the company was "encouraged" by a preliminary analysis done by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration of company data on the importance of one Premarin component.
American Home has argued that the component, delta 8, 9 DHES, should be required in generic copies of Premarin.
An FDA advisory panel in July 1995 declined to make a recommendation on whether to approve a Duramed's generic version of the drug that does not include delta 8, 9 DHES.
At the time, the panel said there was insufficient data to assess whether the ingredient was key to the safety and efficacy of Premarin.
American Home's Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories argued in subsequent data submitted to the FDA that the ingredient was key.
while Duramed and Barr Laboratories Inc, which has also filed a generic version of Premarin with the FDA, have described delta 8, 9 DHES as an "impurity."
"We're pretty encouraged by (the FDA's) perspective on the importance of delta 8, 9," a Wyeth-Ayerst spokeswoman said.
American Home's shares were up 2-3/8 to 62-1/4 in early afternoon trading.
"People are starting to get the feeling that at least this delays (generic Premarin) for a little while longer," said Gruntal Investment Research analyst Adam Greene.
Premarin had worldwide 1995 sales of $912 million, including $760 million in the U.S.
The drug is used to treat the symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, as well as treat a number of conditions including the bone-thinning disease osteoporosis.
Duramed said the company thought, based on its interpretation of the FDA's analysis of the Premarin data, the government body would rule in its favor.
"Duramed is very confident after reviewing the scientific content of the FDA's analysis," Thomas Arington, Duramed's chief executive, said in a statement.
The company spokeswoman said an FDA ruling could come before the end of the year.
Nevertheless, Duramed's shares were off 5/8 to 7-3/4, while Barr Labs was flat at 28-1/4.
